title: The MDX portability scan autolink angle brackets: hazard or not? (design question)
description: Filed from LCLI-697 (gap 2), unstamped for opum-doc. An autolink such as <https://x/> exposes only the inner URL as an mdast text node, so the < and > that MDX would parse are never seen by mdxHazardFindings; the LCLI-663 review probe confirmed it is not caught today. QUESTION: is a bare < or > in an autolink an MDX hazard the scan should flag, like a raw { in prose and as image alt now is (LCLI-697) -- or is NOT flagging it the deliberate ruling? Either way the decision should be recorded, so that not-flagged is a ruling rather than an oversight. UNSTAMPED: no assignee, no acceptance criteria; opum-doc decides.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The MDX portability scan FLAGS an angle-bracket autolink such as <https://x.example/>, and the finding remedy names the portable forms: use [text](url) or a bare URL.
Check: the scan does NOT flag a bare URL or a [text](url) link, so the new arm cannot over-trigger (positive control).
Tests pin both directions: the autolink is flagged; a bare URL and a [text](url) link are not.
